newsitem.title: USA: MCI says files suit against SNET.
newsitem.headline: MCI says files suit against SNET.

text.p: MCI said Tuesday it filed suit with the United States District Court for Connecticut, charging Southern New England Telephone with unfairly restricting customers from changing telephone companies.

MCI said its suit centers on two allegations, including SNET's abuse of its monopoly to restrict customers from making authorized changes in their selection of a long-distance company and SNET's breach of contract by not honoring an agreement to provide MCI certain customer information.
SNET spokesman Kevin Moore said the company's practices were fair.
"This is one way that we can protect our customers from slamming," said Moore. "If a customer does choose to change his carrier they need only to notify us."
Slamming is the practice of carriers changing customers without authorization.

MCI said the primary issue in the suit is that SNET is soliciting customers to sign-up for a freeze on their primary interexchange carrier -- or a lock on their choice of telecommunications carrier -- without disclosing the hurdles they will face when they wish to make authorized changes in their choice of long distance and/or local toll carriers.
MCI also said that under a binding agreement between SNET and MCI, SNET is to provide certain customer information to MCI which it also provides to its own long-distance marketers.
MCI said SNET has stopped providing this information to MCI, creating an unfair advantage for itself and further impeding competition.
